title: Training Vision Transformers to Focus: Emergence of Spatial Attention Head Specialization
claim: Existing models yield ambiguous, near-identical attention across heads; ours steers heads toward diverse, spatially focused, specialized regions.
layout: 2 side-by-side panels, each with 4x4 head grids on top, example below
description: Two hand-drawn-bordered panels sit side by side. The left panel is titled 'DINOv2 Trained Model' and the right is titled 'Our Trained Model'. Each panel holds two 2x8 grids of small viridis-colored heatmaps for attention heads 1-16. The top grids show the ImageNet-average attention. On the left, every head looks like the same blurry central blob. On the right, the heads show distinct, localized patterns: left, right, top, bottom, corner and ring. The bottom grids show attention on a single example image, a photo of four donuts shown in the center between the panels. The left grids look noisy and similar across heads, with a repeated grid-like dot pattern. The right grids show sparse, head-specific focal spots. Bold labels 'ImageNet Average' and 'Example' sit in the center gutter. The eye goes first to the contrast between the uniform blobs on the left and the varied patterns on the right.
caption: Comparison of attention maps produced by the DINOv2 trained model and our trained model. For each model, we show the attention maps averaged over the validation set of the ImageNet-1k [ref] and the attention maps obtained from a single example image. Existing learned perceptual representations (left) in individual attention heads often tend to be ambiguous or overly similar within the example image and across images in the dataset, which limits their interpretability. In contrast, our method (right) selectively steers the focus, leading to the emergence of diverse and spatially focused perceptual capabilities. (Images: Visualization of 16 attention heads in the last layer of trained ViT-L/16-Reg model)
abstract: Self-supervised learning in Vision Transformer models, such as DINO, enables robust visual perception without requiring labeled data by leveraging large-scale image datasets. However, these models lack a focusing mechanism during training, resulting in perceptual representations that are often ambiguous or overly similar. In this work, we introduce two visual focusing loss functions designed to establish correspondence between the model's attention and specific regions within images. Specifically, we leverage the multi-head attention mechanism within the model to selectively steer the model's focus, leading to the emergence of spatial attention head specialization, characterized by diverse and spatially focused perceptual capabilities without requiring annotations. Through both qualitative and quantitative evaluations, we demonstrate that our method substantially increases the spatial selectivity and diversity of attention heads, improving both interpretability and performance on dense prediction tasks such as zero-shot image segmentation.
